newsitem.title: TURKEY: Stronger dollar improves Turkish CB forex position.
newsitem.headline: Stronger dollar improves Turkish CB forex position.

text.p: The dollar's rise against the German mark has been increasing the Turkish central bank's net foreign exchange surplus on its balance sheet, analysts say.

The bank's net foreign exchange surplus -- the difference between its foreign exchange assets and liabilities -- soared by $1.48 billion to $1.59 from $111 million last month when the dollar/mark parity climbed to over 1.6300 from 1.5400 level at end-December.

The bank's foreign exchange assets rose slightly to $19.39 billion from $19.16 billion while the foreign exchange liabilities fell sharply to $17.79 billion at the end of January from $19.05 billion at end-1996.
Analysts say the different structures of the asset and liability parts of the balance sheet helped the central bank widen its foreign currency surplus.
They say the central bank's foreign exchange assets are mainly in dollar and liabilities in the mark.
About 70 percent of the total foreign exchange liabilities consists of foreign currency accounts, held by Turkish workers working abroad, mainly in Germany, at the central bank.
Analysts say the central bank will suffer a shrinkage in its foreign exchange position if the dollar weakens against the mark due to the different compositions of its assets and liabilities.
